output.brief: The evidence points away from the agency operators and the printer firmware. Printer job records show every Veltranol job from 2 Jun to 3 Oct carried a 24-month shelf life and printed correctly. That includes jobs after the firmware change and jobs set up by agency operators. From 4 Oct, every job carried a 36-month shelf life and printed 12 months late. No operator overrides were made, and the printed text matched what the system sent. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol that should only apply from 1 Mar 2027. It appears PackBridge used that value early. That conflicts with the vendor's account, so ask Corvane to explain it. Two lots on Line 1 day shift are also affected and sit in the warehouse, so the fault is not just Line 3 nights. The camera passed everything because it only checks print against the job, not against the batch record. Don't warn or remove the agency staff. Do the following now: fix the Veltranol record, hold all Veltranol lots packed since 4 Oct, add a second-person expiry check against the batch record, and check the other products with future-dated shelf-life edits. Other products are unconfirmed. Keep the camera check on. Confidence is fairly high.
